findings.summary: The new Nudge affordance delivers in-app messages between connected accounts, which contradicts the core scope requirement that direct in-app messaging stay disabled.
findings.evidence: S.webapp.scope: "Direct in-app messaging, subscriptions, digests, media automation and groups must remain disabled in the core scope." vs nudge effects: "Delivers a short \"thinking of you\" card from the owner to the connected person inside the app"

findings.summary: MessageDraft loses its provisional flag and becomes core, but it still sits under the 'provisional (later) entities' grouping and references the still-provisional MediaAsset; the later-capability scope was never amended.
findings.evidence: Diff removes "provisional: true" from entity.MessageDraft, under "# --- provisional (later) entities, spec §5 \"later\" rows"; field approvedAttachments: "list<ref:entity.MediaAsset>" while entity.MediaAsset remains provisional: true

findings.summary: The nudge has no operation and no tie to the revocation policy, so it bypasses server-side authorization and the current-state revocation checks; its criterion also has no sourceRefs to any requirement.
findings.evidence: nudge links only "{ rel: writes, to: entity.MessageDraft }" (no invokes operation, no policy.revocation link); failure lists only "Not available when there is no active Connection"; C.webapp.nudge.single has no sourceRefs, unlike sibling active criteria
